items.title: Danny Barker Interview (Louis Armstrong memorial broadcast), 1971-07-09
items.q: the president of the company, Motion said carry on.

ctx.x: Blueberry Hill, one of the big hit records for which Louis Armstrong is fondly remembered. Those durable vocal cords gave pleasure to a lot of people. And one of them... If that something recent street is jumping in its feet, you will leave. Folks will welcome you and do it up around. It's a friendly old town. So come along down. Come along down. Kill those bells. Time again, when it's spotty crop. Time again, dreams will taunt you. Memories will haunt you.

It is me, oh New Orleans. I said come along down. Come along down. Hear those bells. Time again, when it's spotty crop. Time again, dreams will taunt you. Memories will haunt you. I said come along down. Come along down. I said come along down. Come along down. When it's spotty crop. Time again, dreams will taunt you. Memories will haunt you. Can it be? Yes it be. Use the sounds of me. Song in, Padua. Yeah. Yes it be. Use the sounds of me. Song in, Padua. Well that comes from when I was recording Jeepers…
You remember what the wordless improvisation was when you dropped the music that time?
